name: Drake Industrial Moisture-Wick Work Layer
description:
The cheapest functional base layer available in GLMZ. A single-layer moisture-wicking shirt and legging set that pulls sweat away from the skin and dries within minutes. No smart features, no armor, no sensors — just dry comfort for people who work hard enough to need it.

Sold in packs of three at every supply depot and street market in the lower tiers. The Moisture-Wick Work Layer is the one garment that transcends social boundaries — everyone sweats, and this is the cheapest way to manage it.
what_it_says: You work and you sweat and you spent the minimum to stay dry while doing it.
story_hooks: A bulk shipment of Drake Work Layers destined for a Shelf factory is intercepted — not for the garments, but for something sewn into the linings that the manufacturer didn't put there.

physical_description.visual_profile: A minimalist, utilitarian base layer with a slim athletic fit. The shirt sits close to the torso with short sleeves; leggings reach mid-calf. The overall silhouette is functional and unadorned—no frills, no aesthetic pretension. Worn alone, it reads as working-class practicality; layered under heavier gear, it disappears entirely.
physical_description.fit: Slim, body-hugging compression fit optimized for sweat transfer and thermal regulation. Not tailored—engineered. Slightly tapered at wrists and ankles to prevent bunching.
physical_description.primary_material: Synthetic moisture-wicking blend—likely polyester-nylon composite with minimal elastane. Budget-grade synth-fiber, durable but not luxurious. Designed for durability over aesthetics.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly glossy surface from synthetic coating. Fine ribbed microstructure visible under close inspection—the ribbing channels moisture away. Fabric feels slick and cool to skin, with minimal stretch. No premium softness; purely functional.
physical_description.color_scheme: Utilitarian grays and blacks dominate—charcoal gray shirt, black leggings most common. Occasional neutral variants (navy, dark olive). Minimal branding: small Drake Industrial tab at left chest, nearly invisible unless you know to look.
physical_description.closures: Elastic waistband on leggings (flat, non-adjustable). Shirt has no closures—pullover design. Practical simplicity.
distinctive_features: Flat-lock seams throughout to minimize chafing and reduce moisture pooling at seams
Reinforced gusset at underarm for durability in heavy labor
No pockets, no zippers, no integrated tech
Drake Industrial logo barely visible—minimal branding to reduce manufacturing cost
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4–5. The garment of the working poor and sub-grade labor force. No aspirational design. Sold in bulk at supply depots frequented by gig workers, factory shift crews, and ungoverned zone laborers.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this signals survival and work—honest labor in harsh conditions. Construction crews, maintenance techs, warehouse loaders, street vendors, waste processing. It's the uniform of people who sweat for subsistence. Paradoxically, a Tier 1 corpo in a gym might wear the exact same shirt, but context and layering separate the tiers.
physical_description.condition_typical: Worn in heavy rotation. Fading and slight pilling common after weeks of use. Salt stains visible along neckline and underarms from repeated sweat cycles. Seams hold well due to flat-lock design, but the fabric develops a worn, grayed appearance with age. Often appears patched or mended by the wearer—this is expected.
